a1: Use try/finally for coroutine cleanup; if CancelledError is caught, normally propagate it again after cleanup.
a2: The event loop keeps weak task references; an otherwise unreferenced task may be garbage collected before completion.
a3: TaskGroup cancels remaining tasks when a child fails with an exception other than CancelledError.
a4: TaskGroup and timeout use cancellation internally; swallowing CancelledError can break their behavior.
a5: asyncio.shield protects the inner task from caller cancellation; the caller still receives CancelledError.
a6: After the tasks finish, non-cancellation failures are combined into ExceptionGroup or BaseExceptionGroup and raised.
s1: Use Popen.communicate rather than waiting without draining pipes to avoid blocking on a full pipe.
s2: A communicate timeout does not kill the child; kill it and call communicate again to finish cleanup.
s3: A negative returncode -N means termination by signal N on POSIX.
s4: communicate buffers the read data in memory, so large or unlimited output is unsuitable.
s5: Catching TimeoutExpired and retrying communicate does not lose output.
s6: On POSIX terminate sends SIGTERM whereas kill sends SIGKILL.
On Windows terminate uses TerminateProcess and kill is an alias for terminate.
p1: Following a symlink to an ancestor can recurse forever; Path.walk does not track previously visited directories.
p2: With parents=True, missing parents use default permissions and ignore the requested mode.
p3: Path.walk ignores os.scandir errors by default.
An on_error callback receives OSError and can handle it or re-raise to stop walking.
p4: Path.walk does not follow symbolic links by default; such links are put in filenames.
p5: Path.touch with exist_ok=True succeeds for an existing file and updates its modification time.
p6: Set the case_sensitive keyword argument of Path.glob or rglob explicitly to True or False.
l1: Handlers on a logger and its ancestors may emit the same record multiple times due to propagation.
l2: Logging uses a module lock for shared data and a lock on each handler for underlying IO.
l3: Propagation passes directly to ancestor handlers; ancestor logger levels and filters are not considered.
l4: logging.shutdown flushes and closes all handlers at application exit.
l5: Threading locks are not always re-entrant, so logging from asynchronous signal handlers can be unsafe.
l6: Propagation stops at the first ancestor with propagate=False, after offering the event to its handlers.
